title: A Primitive's defined triggers are never presumed to be the only way to initiate its Process
content:
A.2.2.2.1.1 makes an easily-missed interpretive rule explicit: "The presence of a Time-Based Trigger or Document Update Trigger for a given Process does not necessarily mean such Trigger is the sole means to initiate the Process. For example, an Atlas Document that is external to the Sky Primitives specifications may authorize a Facilitator to manually initiate a process."

Read as a specification, this is a deliberate choice about **closure**. A Process Definition's trigger fields are *sufficient* conditions for initiation, not an *exhaustive* enumeration of them. A reader who treats the schema as complete will wrongly conclude that a Process cannot start outside its listed triggers.

The practical effect is that human discretion remains injectable into any Primitive Process, sourced from documents outside the Primitive specification entirely. That preserves the ability to respond to circumstances the schema did not anticipate — which is why Document Update Triggers can be set to "None" (A.2.2.2.1.1.2) without leaving a Process unreachable.

The cost is that the authoritative answer to "what can start this Process?" is not contained in the Process Definition. Determining it requires searching the wider Atlas for external authorizations, which weakens the schema's promise of self-contained, machine-readable workflows.
description: An external Atlas document can authorize a Facilitator to start a Process manually, so the Time-Based and Document Update Trigger fields describe sufficient conditions, not exhaustive ones.
